target_customer: Pharma partners and patients with immune-mediated diseases such as psoriasis and multiple sclerosis (drug developer, not yet a seller)
problem: Autoimmune diseases are complex and single cytokine drugs address only one signal; Entelexo engineers exosomes to deliver multiple signals to several cell types at once.
business_model: Preclinical biotech developing exosome therapeutics (future licensing or clinical development)

founders.name: Milad Riazifar
education: PhD, Stem Cell Research Center, UC Irvine
founders.background_notes: Source: YC page; exosome research since 2012.

founders.name: Todd Schurr
founders.background_notes: YC page lists cellular biology, electrical engineering and automotive experience; no employers.

founders.name: Cameron Taylor
education: MSE biomedical engineering, University of Michigan (2018)

competitors.name: Codiak BioSciences
competitors.what: Public clinical stage company with engEx engineered exosome platform; lead candidates in oncology, other programs preclinical
competitors.traction_then: Two engineered exosome candidates in solid tumor trials since September 2020; no autoimmune program found
competitors.funding_then: Follow-on offering in February 2021 with $61.9M net proceeds

technical_complexity.rationale: Engineering exosomes that carry multiple signals, manufacturing them and reaching IND is research grade biotech work with long timelines.

defensibility.rationale: A patent on therapeutic delivery platforms was granted in December 2023 per directory data, and clinical development creates barriers, though exosome therapy is early and unproven.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents copying or buying Entelexo; large pharma had little exosome focus then.

market_need_then: Autoimmune diseases such as psoriasis and MS have large patient populations and incomplete treatments, and exosome research was gaining attention, with Codiak already in the clinic in 2020.

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community evidence about the brand was found.

outcome_analysis: Entelexo is a very small preclinical biotech that went through YC in Winter 2021, selected lead candidates in 2022 and began IND enabling animal studies in 2023. Funding found is small and inconsistent across sources, so the lack of larger rounds is not proof of failure but suggests capital is the main constraint for a capital hungry sector. No exit or shutdown was found.
notes: The company site notes a completed pre seed in 2021 without amount or investors; Y Combinator as investor comes from directory listings. CB Insights lists $460K across five rounds, latest a May 2023 convertible note; Wefunder pages show conflicting figures (over $1M raised in one listing, $32,890 in another). All unverified and not recorded. The YC page groups Schurr and Taylor under Former Founders. Patent grant (US 11,851,470 B2, Dec 2023) comes from a search summary only. Name origin not found.
